question: True or false: people in homes with the worst energy ratings tend to burn more heating fuel than the ratings predict?
answer: False. Across 3,400 German homes, occupants used on average 30% less heating energy than their calculated rating, and the gap widened as ratings worsened. Ratings assume every room kept warm; people in draughty houses heat fewer rooms, less. So insulation priced against the rating saves less than forecast: part of the waste was never burned.
move: Measure a saving against what was really used, not what was modelled.
ask: Do I judge my savings by the model or by what I actually used?
trap: Assuming a leaky house wastes even more in practice than on paper.
